bib.title: An Independent Evaluation of ChatGPT on Mathematical Word Problems (MWP)
bib.venue: AAAI Spring Symposium: MAKE 2023 (CEUR Workshop Proceedings)

question: How well does ChatGPT solve math word problems, and which features of a problem predict its failure?
hypothesis: Features of the symbolic equations (counts of unknowns and operations) predict whether ChatGPT fails.
contributions: First independent evaluation of ChatGPT on DRAW-1K
Release of ChatGPT's responses to the 1,000 MWPs
Factors (unknowns, operation counts) linked to higher failure probability
Baseline random forest and XGBoost models predicting ChatGPT correctness

method.summary: The 1,000 DRAW-1K problems were entered into ChatGPT through an unofficial CLI wrapper in three runs (Jan no work, Feb no work, Feb showing work). Responses were classified into four types and failure probability was related to template-equation features; RF and XGBoost predict correctness from ground-truth equation features.
method.task: math word problem solving; failure prediction

datasets.name: DRAW-1K
datasets.size: 1,000 MWPs with answers and template equations
datasets.split: all 1,000 used; five-fold cross-validation for the prediction models
datasets.source: Upadhyay et al. 2016; Upadhyay and Chang; via MWPToolkit

models.name: ChatGPT (Jan 2023 and Feb 2023 versions; ChatGPT Plus for the show-work run)

other.note: OpenAI GPT-3.5 series dialogue model; no API at the time

inference.samples: 1,000 problems; one run per condition (three runs: Jan no work, Feb no work, Feb show work); nondeterminism listed as future work
inference.prompting: Zero-shot. No-work runs append an instruction forcing numbers only; show-work run omits it. Accessed via ChatGPT CLI Python Wrapper (Mahmoud Mabrouk), not an API.

other.interface: web ChatGPT through unofficial wrapper; Feb show-work run used ChatGPT Plus

metrics.name: failure probability
metrics.definition: share of responses that are 'No Solution' or have no correct answer (cases 3 and 4)

metrics.name: response type counts
metrics.definition: all correct (rounding allowed), some correct, No Solution, none correct

metrics.name: R2 of linear fit
metrics.definition: failure probability vs number of add/subtract (or multiply/divide) operations

metrics.name: precision, recall, F1
metrics.definition: of RF and XGBoost predicting incorrect/correct responses, five-fold CV, averaged

eval.protocol: 95% confidence intervals against the prior failure rate; five-fold cross-validation for predictors; features from ground-truth equations (oracle).

results.claim: ChatGPT failed on 84% of DRAW-1K problems when told to give no work, and 20% when it showed work.
results.setup: DRAW-1K, ChatGPT Jan-Feb 2023, no-work vs show-work
results.quote: failing 20% of the time when it provides work compared with 84% when it does not
results.note: Failure = No Solution or none correct

results.claim: Counts of response types per run.
results.setup: order: none correct, No Solution, all correct, some correct
results.table: Table 1, rows by response type, columns Jan No work 831, Feb No work 830, Feb Showing work 186

results.claim: With work shown, ChatGPT fully correct on 51% of problems vs EPT's reported 59%.
results.setup: Feb show-work run; EPT figure reported from other work
results.quote: has fully correct (or rounded) answers 51% of the time, but can be viewed as high as 80% if partially correct answers are included

results.claim: Failure probability rises linearly with number of addition and subtraction operations.
results.setup: Jan no work / Feb no work / Feb show work
results.quote: 𝑅2 = 0.821 for the January experiment, 𝑅2 = 0.870 for the February experiment and 𝑅2 = 0.915 when work was shown

results.claim: Multiplication/division count linearly related to failure only when work is shown.
results.quote: we found a strong linear relationship (𝑅2 = 0.802) for this relationship in the case where work was shown

results.claim: When work is shown, number of unknowns no longer raises failure probability.
Random forest predicting incorrect answers: precision 0.90 recall 0.88 (Jan no work).
results.setup: Jan no-work data, five-fold CV, ground-truth equation features
results.table: Table 2, row Jan. (No work) RF, columns Incorr. Prec. 0.90, Recall 0.88

limits: Each condition run once; nondeterminism not examined (future work).
No-work prompt changed between runs and the authors say the added phrase impacted results, so prompt and showing work are confounded.
Show-work run used ChatGPT Plus, a different access tier.
Predictors use ground-truth equations (oracle); authors say not suitable for practical use.
Only DRAW-1K; unofficial wrapper; model has since changed.
